cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Devices
cards.back: First-class lever: fulcrum between effort and load — e.g. seesaw, scissors. Can provide mechanical advantage or change direction of force.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Devices
cards.back: Second-class lever: load between fulcrum and effort — e.g. wheelbarrow, nutcracker. Always provides mechanical advantage (force multiplier).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Devices
cards.back: Third-class lever: effort between fulcrum and load — e.g. tweezers, human forearm. Provides range of motion, NOT mechanical advantage (speed multiplier).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Devices
cards.back: Gears: toothed wheels transmitting rotary motion — gear ratio = driven/driver. A small driver turning a large driven gear reduces speed but increases torque.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Devices
cards.back: Cams and followers: convert rotary motion to linear/reciprocating — pear cam (slow rise, quick drop), eccentric cam (constant rise/fall), snail cam (gradual rise, sudden drop).

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For mechanical device questions: 1) Identify the device type, 2) Label fulcrum/effort/load on a diagram, 3) Apply the correct formula, 4) Interpret the result (what does the number mean in context?). Always state the formula before substituting values.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: All levers give you a mechanical advantage — they always make the load easier to lift. Correct: Only first-class and second-class levers can provide mechanical advantage.
